title: Special Assets Standard — Default-Interest Trigger by Loan Seasoning and Default Record (Farm Real Estate Loans)
content:
**Standard.** The trigger days for default-rate interest on a Farm Real Estate Loans installment depend on the loan's seasoning and its record: a loan at least 36 months old at the installment's due date that has had no default-rate interest entry in the last 60 months is allowed the first-episode trigger of 75 days; a loan at least 36 months old at the due date that has had a default-rate interest entry in the last 60 months is held to the repeat trigger of 45 days; any other loan uses the product's default-interest trigger days.

## What the records show

- **Seasoning** — the loan's age in months from its closing date to the due date of the installment considered.
- **Record** — the default-rate interest entries (interest entries marked as default-rate interest) in the loan's transaction history dated in the last 60 months.

## The ladder

| Loan age at the installment's due date | Default-rate interest entries in the last 60 months | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 36 months or more | none | first-episode trigger: 75 days |
| 36 months or more | one or more | repeat trigger: 45 days |
| less than 36 months | none | the product's default-interest trigger days |
| less than 36 months | one or more | the product's default-interest trigger days |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical loans)

- A loan that is exactly 36 months old at the due date, with no default-rate interest entry in the last 60 months, is allowed 75 days; a loan 35 months old with the same clean record uses the product's default-interest trigger days.
- A loan 80 months old whose only default-rate interest entry is dated 59 months ago has an entry in the last 60 months and is held to 45 days; if that entry were dated 61 months ago, the loan would have none in the window and be allowed 75 days.

## Points of judgement

**Does the first-episode trigger depend on whether the member has ever had default interest?** Only on the last 60 months: an entry older than that does not count.

**Which age counts?** The age at the installment's due date, not today's age.
